Thanks, Jordan. Quick read — overall doable but a few items need to be resolved before procurement signs off:

1) Data residency / retention: procurement requires confirmation that PII-enriched records are deleted within 90 days of request and that backups are rotated per their policy. Please request the formal retention SLA from Mercury.
2) Pricing guardrails: we prefer a committed-MPU (monthly processing units) model with an overage cap at 120% of committed. The per-call overage rates in the proposal look punitive.
3) Payment terms: Net 30 preferred; 10% off for pre-pay is fine but we need a short-circuit clause to avoid auto-renewal without notification.
4) Compliance evidence: please send latest SOC2 Type II and penetration test summary.

I attached a short procurement checklist with the items we typically escalate. Sam — could you confirm items 1 and 3 above and share SOC2? If Mercury can accept the committed-MPU with a 120% cap and Net 30, procurement can sign.

Monica
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Jordan/Monica — thanks for the clear notes. Short answers:

1) Data retention: Mercury confirms deletion-on-request within 90 days and a backup rotation policy — I’ve attached the SOC2 Type II report and a short DPA addendum clause that reflects the 90-day retention.
2) Pricing model: We can offer a committed Monthly Processing Unit (MPU) option at the same effective monthly cost as the 12-month pre-pay, with a 120% overage cap. That will replace the punitive per-call overage line items.
3) Payment terms: Contracts team is okay with Net 30 for enterprise customers; we’ll add a 30-day non-auto-renewal notification clause.

I’ve uploaded the updated proposal and pushed it to DocuSign for the 12-month committed-MPU pre-pay option with the agreed contract language: https://docusign.com/s/abc123-renewal

If that looks good, please sign and I’ll ensure we schedule a short kickoff to confirm data transfer paths and test enrichment jobs so there’s no downtime.
